clue.text: Attacks the underworld? That really is surprising.

parts.note: attacks from the air are bombs, used here as a verb
hell is the underworld of the dead

explanation.surface: Someone muses about raids on the underworld and finds the idea astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is a piece of shocking news, something that comes as a great surprise.

clue.text: Well disposed to organise noble event

indicators.note: organising the letters puts them into a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone kindly offers to arrange a grand event for the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kind and charitable in outlook is what it means to wish others well.

clue.text: Marvellous thing, keeping motorway clear somehow

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the next word are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: It would be a wonder if the motorway stayed free of traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' is a link here; MI comes first and RACLE, the anagram of CLEAR made by 'somehow', follows it. The M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is a wonder, an event so extraordinary it seems beyond nature.

clue.text: Long oar's point getting stuck in ooze

indicators.note: a piece that gets stuck in another sits inside it

parts.note: to ooze is to seep slowly out
W, west, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The tip of a long oar becomes trapped in the mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' means a compass point, here W for west.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is a long oar used for steering or rowing a large boat.

clue.text: From both poles, sleds seen abandoned? No conclusion!

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters run riot

parts.note: the North and South poles are N and S

explanation.surface: Polar explorers spot sledges left behind at either end of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' is the anagram signal for N and S plus SLEDS SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no conclusion goes on for ever, the state of being infinite.

clue.text: Member of a cricket side

definitions.meaning: the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's ..., also called on side

explanation.surface: Someone plays for a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into off side and the other side, named after the batsman's lower limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a member of the body, and the on side of a cricket field takes the same name.

clue.text: Drive mile — make a mess of parking inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece is placed within the other
messing up the letters jumbles them into a new order

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A driver covers a mile but bungles the parking at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a mess of' turns MILE into IMEL; 'inside' puts P within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to push or urge forward, as a force propels something onward.

clue.text: By no means off-colour

parts.note: being far from off-colour means being in excellent health, and the idiom for that names a rosy shade

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in very good health, the opposite of feeling off-colour.

clue.text: Wan child in large overcoat

parts.note: wan means pale
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A pale little child is swamped by a big coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose outer coat, an old-fashioned name for a roomy greatcoat.

clue.text: Second eleven initially applying superior technique in final

indicators.note: second picks out the second letter of the word eleven
initially takes the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A reserve team wins the final with better skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' looks like a reserve team, but 'Second' takes L from 'eleven'.
explanation.definitionFit: Last and final both describe the one that comes at the end.

clue.text: Courage never faltering

indicators.note: faltering means unsteady, so the letters of the word stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A brave person who never wavers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is boldness, the steadiness needed to face danger.

clue.text: Figure it is about a quid for the drug

parts.note: to figure something out is to understand it, which in slang is to dig it

indicators.note: about means the outer words go around the inner pieces

parts.note: a quid is a pound, written L from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone calculates the price of a medicine at about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' is a verb, understand, slang DIG; 'about' puts A and L inside IT IS. Quid is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is a heart medicine made from foxglove leaves.

clue.text: Not in charge, but he'll get to pen directives, somehow

definitions.text: Not in charge, but he'll get to

indicators.note: somehow means the letters get rearranged in some fashion

explanation.surface: A deputy, not yet in charge, will one day write the orders.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a deputy who will take over only if the leader goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy leader is not in charge but would take over should the president die or leave.

clue.text: ′ A hindrance, having a lot of luggage

parts.note: an impediment is a hindrance or obstacle

explanation.surface: Carrying too many bags is a real hindrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The A from the start of the clue goes at the end; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedimenta are baggage and equipment, things that slow a traveller down.

clue.text: Lost posy in Morris dancing upon my word, I could be made to pay!

definitions.text: upon my word, I could be made to pay!

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A morris dancer drops a bunch of flowers mid-jig and fears a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is an English folk dance. 'Lost' is a link word in the anagram's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A promissory note is a written promise to pay, binding the signer.

clue.text: Port with cheese souffle provided for hangers-on

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship, abbreviated L

indicators.note: a souffle whips its ingredients up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A dinner menu offering port with a cheese souffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink served with cheese; it is the ship's left side, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeches are parasites that cling on, so people who sponge off others get the name.

clue.text: Stuffing that may be curried

parts.note: curry here means to groom a horse with a comb, not to cook spicily; the filling once came off such animals

explanation.definitionFit: Hair from a horse's mane or tail was used to stuff mattresses and furniture.

clue.text: Bow tie for an artist

definitions.meaning: a rope at the front of a boat used to tie it up
someone who makes pictures in oils or watercolour

explanation.surface: A neckwear choice for someone arty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow tie' is not neckwear: it is a mooring rope at a boat's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's mooring line at the bow and a person who paints share the same name.

clue.text: Treen turned, in Utah, from this source?

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
turned means the letters are worked into a different order, like wood on a lathe

parts.note: UT is the postal abbreviation for Utah

explanation.surface: Wooden bowls turned on a lathe in Utah come from a particular tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Treen means small wooden objects, which are turned on a lathe; 'turned' is the anagram signal giving NTREE, with UT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden ware may be carved from a hazel or walnut, the source of the timber.

clue.text: Buck swimming to cross over. to kid's food-treat

indicators.note: swimming letters float about into a new arrangement

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A male deer swims across a river towards a child's snack box.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuck box is a British boarding-school child's box of sweets and snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is British slang for snacks, kept by schoolchildren in a box from home.

clue.text: Duchy out-moded in United Kingdom

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
out means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A duchy seems old-fashioned in modern Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out-moded' looks like one word, but 'out' signals an anagram of MODED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dukedom is the territory or rank of a duke, the same as a duchy.

clue.text: Buck's partner fell — now is turned into gloves?

parts.note: a doe is the female partner of a buck deer
a fell is an animal's hide

explanation.surface: A female deer's skin is made into gloves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb, fell down; it is a noun meaning hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft leather from a deer is used to make fine gloves.

clue.text: Should make a profit from Cheddar gorge?

definitions.text: Should make a profit from Cheddar gorge?

parts.words: Should make a profit from Cheddar gorge?
parts.note: Cheddar Gorge is a beauty spot in Somerset, but read as stuffing yourself with cheddar it is good business for those selling it

explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers selling cheese profit when people gorge on cheddar.

clue.text: Egg applied — it's used for radiotherapy

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
something applied is put on

explanation.surface: An egg is put on as a treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Niton is an old name for radon, the radioactive gas once used in cancer treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon, once called niton, was used as a radiation source in treating cancer.

clue.text: Good meeting-place for a driver

definitions.meaning: a society's premises where members meet
a golf stick for long shots off the tee

explanation.surface: A friendly place for motorists to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A society's premises and a golf stick both share the same name.

clue.text: Scales first ridge in a storm -'all in the job!.

parts.note: Libra is the scales of the zodiac

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the following word
a storm tosses the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber scales a ridge in a storm and shrugs it off as part of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' makes IAN from IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of books would say books are everything in their work.

clue.text: Is duck penned in this place?

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a duck is kept in a pen here.
explanation.walkthrough: Ios is a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ios is a Greek island, a place in the Cyclades.

clue.text: Holiday ending, took off for the capital

indicators.note: off means the letters go wrong and are rearranged
ending takes the last letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A holiday ends with a trip to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges Y and TOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

clue.text: Dog one might take for a pug?

definitions.text: one might take for a pug?
definitions.meaning: pug is short for pugilist, a fighter in the ring

explanation.surface: A dog someone mistakes for a pug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pug' looks like the dog breed but is short for pugilist.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of dog and a prizefighter share the name.

clue.text: Sluggishness of animal carrying girl

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An animal is seen carrying a girl on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is a link: the girl follows the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnancy is the state of not moving or developing, inactivity.
